response.title: how many watts for home backup generator

For a typical American home, a backup generator rated at 7,500–12,000 watts (7.5–12 kW) can power essential appliances, while 18,000–26,000 watts (18–26 kW) is a common range for whole-house backup.

My recommendation

For most homes:

8–10 kW: Good for essential backup.

14–18 kW: Good balance between cost and convenience.

The generator must also support the home's voltage requirements, usually 120/240 V in the US. A proper transfer switch or interlock is essential to prevent dangerous backfeeding.

markup:
For a typical American home, a backup generator rated at **7,500–12,000 watts (7.5–12 kW)** can power essential appliances, while **18,000–26,000 watts (18–26 kW)** is a common range for whole-house backup.

## Generator size by home needs

| Backup needs | Recommended generator size |
|---|---|
| Refrigerator, lights, Wi-Fi, phone charging | 2,000–4,000 W |
| Essentials + microwave + furnace blower | 5,000–7,500 W |
| Essentials + well pump or small central AC | 7,500–12,000 W |
| Most household circuits + central AC | 12,000–20,000 W |
| Whole house, including large AC and appliances | 20,000–26,000 W |
| Large home with multiple AC units or electric heating | 26,000–40,000+ W |

## Typical appliance power consumption

| Appliance | Running watts | Starting watts (approx.) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Refrigerator | 150–800 | 600–2,000 |
| Wi-Fi router | 10–30 | — |
| LED lights (10 bulbs) | 80–120 | — |
| Microwave | 1,000–1,500 | — |
| Gas furnace blower | 400–800 | 800–1,600 |
| Central AC (3 ton) | 2,000–4,000 | 5,000–10,000+ |
| Electric water heater | 4,500 | — |
| Electric dryer | 4,000–6,000 | — |
| EV charger (Level 2) | 7,000–11,500 | — |

Starting watts matter because motors and compressors can briefly draw much more power when switching on.

## My recommendation

For most homes:

- **8–10 kW:** Good for essential backup.
- **14–18 kW:** Good balance between cost and convenience.
- **22–26 kW:** Good starting point for whole-house backup, depending on your electrical loads.

The generator must also support the home's voltage requirements, usually 120/240 V in the US. A proper transfer switch or interlock is essential to prevent dangerous backfeeding.

## Let me size one for your home

<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <form gap={3} onSubmit={()=>GenUI.issueNewTurn("Recommend a home backup generator wattage for my "+sqft+" sq ft home, AC: "+ac+", heating: "+heat+", backup goal: "+scope+". Include running and starting watt considerations.")}>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>Home size</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={sqft} onChange={setSqft}>
        <radio value="under 1500">Under 1,500 sq ft</radio>
        <radio value="1500-2000">1,500–2,000 sq ft</radio>
        <radio value="2000-3000">2,000–3,000 sq ft</radio>
        <radio value="over 3000">Over 3,000 sq ft</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <divider color="subtle"/>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>Air conditioning</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={ac} onChange={setAc}>
        <radio value="central">Central AC</radio>
        <radio value="window or mini split">Window AC / mini-split</radio>
        <radio value="none">No AC</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <divider color="subtle"/>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>Home heating</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={heat} onChange={setHeat}>
        <radio value="gas">Natural gas</radio>
        <radio value="electric or heat pump">Electric / heat pump</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <divider color="subtle"/>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>What do you want to power?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={scope} onChange={setScope}>
        <radio value="essentials">Essentials only</radio>
        <radio value="whole">Entire house</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <button block submit>Calculate recommended generator size <icon name="arrow-right" inline/></button>
  </form>
</box>
